=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text first "first 25 pernicious numbers:"
text range "pernicious numbers from 888888877 to 888888888:"
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
fn popc n ulong to ulong
c = ulong 0
v = n
while gt v 0 bound 64
c = add c and v 1
v = shr v 1
end
ret c
end
note a pernicious number has a prime population count; counts here are at most 30, so trial division is enough
fn isprime n ulong to bool
if lt n 2
ret false
end
d = ulong 2
while le mul d d n bound 8
if eq rem n d 0
ret false
end
d = add d 1
end
ret true
end
fn main to int
emit first
c = ulong 0
n = ulong 1
while lt c 25 bound 100
if isprime popc n
emit sp
emitu n
c = add c 1
end
n = add n 1
end
emit nl
emit range
for i ulong 12
n = add 888888877 i
if isprime popc n
emit sp
emitu n
end
end
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
first 25 pernicious numbers: 3 5 6 7 9 10 11 12 13 14 17 18 19 20 21 22 24 25 26 28 31 33 34 35 36
pernicious numbers from 888888877 to 888888888: 888888877 888888878 888888880 888888883 888888885 888888886
</pre>
